messages:
ali: quick summary — ran a 2h sim of the continuous-batcher with kernel-hinting + prefetch-on-kv-hit enabled. workload: 60/40 short/long. results look mixed, filing here before digging deeper.

mira: ok, what stood out?

ali: two things: 1) average latency p95 for short requests dropped ~7% when we preferred FP16 fused matmul kernels for 128-256 seq, 2) tail spikes around cache-eviction windows where admission started issuing soft 429s.

jia: can you paste the perf numbers and config used?

ali: sure — config snippet:
```
batch_window_ms: 12
max_batch_tokens: 4096
token_budget_target: 2800
kernel_hint_order: [fused_fp16, matmul_opt, fallback_fp32]
kv_prefetch: true
admission.soft_limit_pct: 0.92
soft_429_ramp_ms: 150
```

ali: perf table (avg across 2h):
- short reqs: p50 12ms -> 11.2ms, p95 48ms -> 44.9ms
- long reqs: p50 92ms -> 90ms, p95 320ms -> 305ms
- overall token/sec +3.4%
- but 429 events: 4.2k (spiky, concentrated at ~minute boundaries)

ryan: spike timing matches our KV eviction sweep that runs every minute — when cache misses spike, we fall back to slower kernels and admission hits the soft threshold.

mira: do we know why kernel selection took the slower path? should be preferring fused_fp16 for short-seq.

ali: checked traces — when prefetch misses happen, the kernel selector backs off to matmul_opt because KV fetch latency pushed estimated end-to-end beyond our batch_window_ms. selector code currently uses a simplistic cost model: compute_cost + est_kv_latency. when est_kv_latency > 18ms, it prefers matmul_opt.

jia: maybe we should add a hysteresis term to avoid flipping kernels on transient kv latency blips. a short-term moving median of kv latency could stabilize selection.

ryan: also admission currently uses a token_budget_target computed from recent token throughput without accounting for batched KV impact. when a batch contains several cache misses token cost per request rises and we hit soft_limit_pct faster.

mira: proposal: 1) add 5s EWMA for KV latency used by kernel selector, 2) tag batches with kv_miss_count and penalize token_budget_target by a factor proportional to misses, 3) smooth soft_429 ramp policy to spread rejections rather than burst at minute boundaries.

ali: I ran a quick smoke with EWMA=5s and kv miss penalty = 0.6 * miss_count, results: 429s dropped to ~900, tail latency slightly higher for short p95 (+1.5%) but much less spike variance.

perf-bot: profile upload complete: https://perf.internal/redwood/1749999999/flame-agg.html (contains flamegraph, KV wait histogram, kernel-switch timeline)

jia: nice — can we get a small synthetic that reproduces the minute-aligned sweep? maybe run a workload where 1 in 8 short requests is artificially cache-miss at minute boundaries.

ali: yes, I have a harness. command I used:
```sh
./run_harness --mix short:0.6,long:0.4 --kv-pattern minute_sweep --duration 7200 --seed 42
```

ryan: follow-ups: I'll add the EWMA knob to kernel selector and expose kernel-hint diagnostic in traces. jia, can you add kv_miss_count to the batch metric and compute adjusted token_budget in the dashboard?

mira: and I'll prototype changing soft_429_ramp_ms to a percentile-based backoff (e.g., when p95 token usage > target -> ramp to 250ms over 60s rather than immediate bursts).

ali: timeline: PRs for EWMA + diagnostics by EOD tomorrow, dashboard metric by jia in 2 days, soft_429 ramp experiment in staging next week. if staging looks good we can ship to canary.

deploy-bot: canary deployment created: dedicated-cluster-canary-13 for branch/ewma-kernel-hint (expires in 3 days).

mira: quick note — watch cost implications of preferring fused_fp16: may slightly increase memory pressure and kernel queueing on some hardware profiles. include a kernel-queue-length monitor in the canary run.

ali: good point. I'll add kernel_queue_len and per-kernel concurrency to the canary dashboard.

jia: action items summarized: [ali] add harness commands and share seed, [ryan] EWMA + trace, [mira] soft_429 experiment plan, [jia] dashboard metrics. I'll sync with infra to ensure the minute_sweep generator is available in staging.

ryan: thanks — will post PR link when ready.

ali: thanks all. short follow-up: we should also run the same sim with quantized kernels; earlier runs hinted different behavior (more sensitive to kv latency). let's add that to the test matrix.

mira: agreed.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from jia, ryan, mira)
